rules.rule: Check for known diabetes when fingerprick glucose is low or high
rules.problem: Type and check_for are right, but the trigger covers only < 4 and >= 11.1. The page branches on known diabetes in every band ('3-6 (4-6 if known diabetes)', '6.1-11: If known diabetes, give routine care'), so the status is needed at any glucose value; harmless as written because the middle bands are not encoded, but narrower than the page.

rules.rule: Check for urgent signs when fingerprick glucose is 11.1 or more
Check urine for ketones when fingerprick glucose is 11.1 or more
rules.problem: The page checks urine ketones only on the 'No' branch of 'Check if patient needs urgent attention'; the task fires on glucose >= 11.1 alone. Clinically harmless (an urgent patient goes to the fluids/refer box either way) but the and-structure drops a conjunct.

rules.rule: Check for symptoms of diabetes when glucose is 11.1 or more without ketones
rules.problem: Same dropped conjunct: the page reaches 'does patient have symptoms of diabetes?' only after no urgent signs and no ketones. Also the page asks the same symptom question in the fasting-glucose >= 7 branch, which no rule triggers.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable hypoglycaemia from fingerprick glucose
Diagnose probable diabetes from random glucose 11.1 or more with symptoms
rules.problem: Probable is the right level ('Diagnose diabetes'), but the page's diagnostic logic is only partly encoded: (1) 'If < 35 years, type 1 diabetes likely. Refer.' is a 'likely' on the page and has no probable rule for (snomed_concept "Diabetes mellitus type 1" "disorder") gated on age < 35; (2) the fasting-glucose route to 'Diagnose diabetes' (fasting >= 7 with symptoms, or fasting >= 7 repeated 1 week later) and 'Patient has impaired fasting glucose' (fasting 6.1-6.9) are absent; (3) the rule requires no ketonuria but not the absence of the red-box urgent signs, although the page requires both before it reaches this question.

rules.rule: Urgent: glucose 11.1 or more with danger signs
rules.problem: Level Urgent matches 'Check if patient needs urgent attention' and 'Refer urgently'; all ten red-box items present. See c052 for the dehydration footnote criteria.

rules.rule: Urgent: glucose 11.1 or more with urine ketones

summary: No claim is invented or wrong: every condition traces to the page, the thresholds, directions and units are right, and both probable diagnoses are definitive on the page. The most consequential gap is that the diabetes diagnosis rule encodes only the random-glucose route and omits the page's other 'likely'/diagnostic outcomes (type 1 diabetes likely if under 35; diabetes from fasting glucose >= 7 twice or with symptoms; impaired fasting glucose), and the ketone, symptom and diagnosis rules drop the page's 'no urgent signs' conjunct. Two concept-level imprecisions: 'Confusion' is rendered as Clouded consciousness where Acute confusion exists, and the priority rule's Dehydration ignores footnote 7's BP < 90/60 and pulse >= 100 criteria.
